issues.legal_issue: The twin conditions for bail under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act do not displace the principle that bail is the rule and jail is the exception, and prolonged pre-trial incarceration with no likelihood of a timely trial may justify conditional liberty consistently with Article 21.

At the bail stage under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the court need not decide guilt beyond reasonable doubt but must assess whether reasonable grounds support the belief that the accused is not guilty and is unlikely to commit an offence while on bail.

The presumption under Section 24 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act arises only after the prosecution establishes the foundational facts, including the existence of proceeds of crime and the accused’s connection with them.

A statement recorded under Section 50 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act from a person in judicial custody in another proceeding investigated by the same agency is inadmissible against its maker under Section 25 of the Evidence Act.
A co-accused’s statement is not substantive evidence against another accused and may be used only to lend assurance to independently established evidence.
